inputs: Incoming scene containing the objects in their final arrangement
One separate cutout/mask per object, extracted from or matched to the incoming scene
Object entrance order and final alignment targets
Background-switch time and per-object white-blip timing
recipe.preparation: Extract each object independently; align its settled size/position with the incoming scene; build staggered entrances, one background switch, and alpha-confined white blips as one sequence
success_criteria: Objects enter separately over the outgoing shot, land without jumping when the background switches, then blip white within their own silhouettes. Reuse with a different number and type of objects.

inputs: Incoming shot with an isolatable subject
Matching original-color and white alpha mattes
recipe.preparation: Continuous variant: align white and original-color alpha mattes to the incoming picture. At 30 fps, cover all five lead-in frames: white for two frames, color for three, then switch scene. No empty frame between masks. Keep each matte native and editable. See anderson-taii-transitions.md for reference-pulse and continuous variants. For consecutive handoffs, invoke mask-glitch with ordered shots and derive one coordinated chain schedule; masks remain separate editable rows.
success_criteria: Every lead-in frame contains the white silhouette or original-color subject mask; no disappearance before the incoming scene.
White and colour masks share alpha and geometry and match the incoming picture; preserve unchanged sources and editable layers.
Verify on another incoming subject before promoting the recipe to complete.

success_criteria: Match the chosen negative/original timing map
Keep the negative treatment scoped to the portrait

observations: The technique was recreated once on private footage with source and effect layers stored separately; that example is not redistributed, so no recreation is packaged here.
limitations: No redistributable recreation is packaged yet; recreate on cleared footage before marking this partial again.
